provenance.instrument: Borough of Lansdale Code Chapter 405 Zoning (Ord. No. 1393, 11-16-1988, as amended), as published on eCode360
provenance.status_detail: eCode360 code date 2026-05-20 (breadcrumb). New Laws for Chapter 405 on 2026-11-14: Ord. 2012 'Residential B&C amendments 8.19.2026(A)', listed as adopted 2026-11-19, and Ord. 2013 'TOD text amendment', adopted 2026-08-19. PDF only, not read.
provenance.code_current_through_note: eCode360 breadcrumb 'Code 2026-05-20'. Two 2026 zoning amendments (Residential B and C, TOD) are listed as New Laws, not yet in the code text.
provenance.code_caution: Ord. 2012 (Residential B and C amendments) is listed as a New Law for Chapter 405 and was not read (PDF only). It is listed as adopted on Nov 19, 2026, although its title says 8.19.2026. Search excerpts show it rewrites the Class B and C use and dimensional tables, adds a stacked townhome, and changes the row on conversion of single-family detached dwellings (to 'other non-residential' uses). The B and C figures and the duplex note below may change. Ord. 2013 amends the TOD overlay text.
checks: 'Accessory dwelling units shall be permitted by right attached to or contained within single-family detached homes only' (405-1913B). Not in a separate building, not joined by a corridor or breezeway (405-1913E)

Single-family detached dwellings are permitted in Class A, B and C Residential and in LPO (405-402, 405-502, 405-602, 405-1001A), not in Residential Apartment, Professional Office A or Professional Office B (405-700, 405-800, 405-900). Other districts were not read
Occupants are limited to the parents, grandparents, step-parents or step-grandparents of the occupants of the house, or the spouse, sibling or partner of one of them. At most two people (405-1913G)
The house is owner-occupied and the owner's primary residence. The unit may not be rented (405-1913F, I)

A deed restriction is recorded with the Montgomery County Recorder of Deeds. A license to operate is renewed every year by January 1, with inspections twice a year. The second kitchen is removed within six months after the approved occupant leaves (405-1913A, H, J)

One more off-street parking space, unless the house already has at least one space beyond its own requirement. Utilities are routed through the house. A separate entrance that does not face the street, no separate address or mailbox (405-1913B, D, K, L)

Lot area per dwelling unit: Class A 9,000 sq ft (standard option), Class B 5,600, Class C 4,500 for a single-family detached dwelling. These standard figures apply to redevelopment 'at a density greater than existed prior' (405-504, 405-604). Alterations that do not increase density use the block-median figures (405-506A(2), 405-606A(2)). 405-1913 calls the ADU an accessory use that may not be rented 'as an apartment or separate dwelling unit', and the house reverts to 'a single-family dwelling unit' when the license ends (405-1913B, I, J(7)). Whether the ADU counts as a dwelling unit for lot area is not said. Ask the Code Enforcement Officer
An addition visible on the front facade of the house (such as a second-story addition) needs Article XXXVII infill design review (405-405A(2), 405-507A(2), 405-607A(2))
In LPO only 'A single accessory use' is allowed with the house (405-1001B). LPO lot and yard rules are those of the most restrictive abutting residential district (405-1002)
TOD overlay: single-family detached dwellings within an approved TOD development and 'Accessory residential uses or buildings' are listed (405-3202A, K). Ord. 2013 amends this text and was not read
An accessory building is 'subordinate, uninhabitable' by definition, so a unit in a detached garage or outbuilding is not allowed (405-201)
provenance.notes: Zoning office: Borough of Lansdale Department of Code Enforcement. Read on eCode360 (LA0393) in a browser, one page at a time, on 2026-11-14. Code search (all content, New Laws included) for 'accessory apartment', 'accessory dwelling', 'in-law', ECHO, 'elder cottage', granny, 'family dwelling', relative, 'housekeeping unit', caretaker, 'tenant house' and 'guest house' found 405-1913 and the ADU definition (405-201). Neither 2026 New Law shows an 'accessory dwelling' hit. Read in full: 405-1913, the definitions page (ADU, accessory building), Class A, B and C Residential (Articles IV to VI), Residential Apartment (Article VII), Professional Office A and B (Articles VIII, IX) and LPO (Article X). TOD overlay (Article XXXII) read for its use list only. Not read: Commercial, Business, B-2, Industrial and the other overlays, accessory structures (405-1904) and parking (405-1703). Ord. 2012 and 2013 are PDF only and were not opened. Fix round 2026-11-14 after an independent review: scope now names PO-A, PO-B (not permitted) and LPO (permitted), PO-B conversion read in full, RA duplex added, Ord. 2012 caution rewritten, density reading quotes and design review added.

term.note: 'A suite attached to or contained within the principal dwelling unit on a lot that houses certain family members of the occupant(s) of the principal dwelling unit, and may contain separate cooking facilities' (Ord. No. 2018-1907).

status.note: By right, attached to or inside a single-family detached home, only for parents, grandparents and step-relatives of the household (or their spouse, sibling or partner), at most two people, owner-occupied, not rented.

scope_by_use.note: The ADU is allowed with single-family detached homes only. Class A, B and C and LPO list single-family detached dwellings. Residential Apartment, Professional Office A and Professional Office B do not (PO-B lists a conversion of a single-family dwelling, not the house itself). Other districts' use lists were not read.

status_outside.note: Where single-family detached dwellings are not permitted, no ADU rule applies.

path.note: 'Permitted by right.' A recorded deed restriction and an accessory dwelling unit license to operate, renewed every year.

fallback_path.note: Relief from a district rule is a variance from the Zoning Hearing Board.

value.name: Two-family duplex dwelling in Class B or C Residential
value.conditions: Two-family duplex dwellings are permitted. Lot area per dwelling unit 5,600 sq ft (B) or 4,500 sq ft (C), side yards 8 ft, rear 20 ft. 'Conversion of single-family detached dwelling to other uses' is listed as not permitted.
value.note: Lot figures are two units at the per-unit area. 'Conversion of single-family detached dwelling to other uses' is listed as not permitted, so today this is a path for a new duplex, not for converting a house. Ord. 2012 (not read) changes that row to conversion 'to other non-residential' uses and rewrites the B and C tables, so this may change. Ask the Code Enforcement Officer.

value.name: Conversion of a single-family dwelling to apartment conversion units in Professional Office District B
value.conditions: An existing single-family dwelling converted to apartment conversion units. At least 1,500 sq ft of lot area for each unit (3,000 sq ft for two). The parking requirements of the chapter met for each unit. Yards: front 15 ft, two sides of 6 ft each, rear 50 ft. Units meet Chapter 146, Building Construction, Article I. Buildings, parking and other impervious cover at most 75% of the lot. Height 40 ft.
value.note: 405-901 also asks 7,500 sq ft 'for all other permitted uses' within the district. Whether that reaches a conversion, which has its own 1,500 sq ft per unit figure in 405-900E, is not said. Ask the Code Enforcement Officer.

value.name: Two-family duplex dwelling in the Residential Apartment District
value.conditions: Two-family duplex dwellings are a permitted use. Lot 6,000 sq ft, width 60 ft at the street line, front 30 ft, two sides of 10 ft, rear 50 ft, height 40 ft, impervious cover at most 75%.
value.note: Single-family detached dwellings are not a listed RA use.

zoning_districts.note: Districts read that permit single-family detached dwellings.

value.condition: Occupants limited to the parents, grandparents, step-parents or step-grandparents of the occupants of the house, or the spouse, sibling or partner of one of those relatives. At most two people.
The house is owner-occupied and the owner's primary residence. The unit may not be leased or rented.

Deed restriction recorded with the Montgomery County Recorder of Deeds. Annual license to operate (by January 1), inspections twice a year, owner reimburses enforcement costs. The second kitchen is removed within six months after the approved occupant leaves.

Attached and interconnected with the house, any connecting door open from both sides. A separate entrance that does not face the street (on a corner lot, not the street the main entrance faces). No separate address or mailbox. Outside changes keep the look of a single-family detached house. The addition meets the house's dimensional rules.
All utilities for the unit are routed through the house.
An addition visible on the front facade of the house, such as a second-story addition, needs Article XXXVII infill design review.
In LPO only a single accessory use is allowed with the house, so the ADU would be that one accessory use (no accessory professional office with it).

districts_read_no_listing.note: Use lists read. None lists single-family detached dwellings or an ADU.

types_allowed.note: 'Attached to or contained within single-family detached homes only.' 'Shall not be located in a separate freestanding building joined to the principal dwelling by a corridor or breezeway.'

owner_occupancy.note: 'The principal dwelling unit shall [be] owner-occupied, and shall be the primary residence of the owner of the property.'

occupancy.value: At most two people: parents, grandparents, step-parents or step-grandparents of the occupants of the house, or the spouse, sibling or partner of one of them.

max_adus.note: 'An accessory dwelling unit' with the house. No number is stated.

spaces_required.note: 'An accessory dwelling unit requires one new, additional off-street parking space.' Not needed if the house already has at least one space beyond its own requirement.

min_lot_sqft.note: Standard option, per dwelling unit, where two or fewer homes are on the block. Where more than two are, the block median lot area governs (405-404A). Width 60 ft. Impervious 45%.

setback_front_ft.note: 24 ft minimum, 30 ft maximum. On a block with homes, the block median.

lot_area_per_unit_sqft.note: 'The minimum lot area shall be 9,000 square feet per dwelling unit.' Applies to the ADU only if it counts as a dwelling unit. 405-1913 calls it an accessory use not rented 'as an apartment or separate dwelling unit'. Ask.

min_lot_sqft.note: Single-family detached, per dwelling unit. Width 45 ft. Existing homes use the block median (405-506). Impervious 75%.

setback_front_ft.note: Block median of permitted uses, 24 ft where the block has no homes.

lot_area_per_unit_sqft.note: Applies to redevelopment 'at a density greater than existed prior'. Applies to the ADU only if it counts as a dwelling unit. 405-1913 calls it an accessory use not rented 'as an apartment or separate dwelling unit' and additions without a density increase use the block-median figures (405-506A(2)). Ask.

min_lot_sqft.note: Single-family detached, per dwelling unit. Width 32 ft. Existing homes use the block median (405-606). Impervious 75%.

setback_front_ft.note: Block median of permitted uses, 24 ft where the block has no homes.

lot_area_per_unit_sqft.note: Applies to redevelopment 'at a density greater than existed prior'. Applies to the ADU only if it counts as a dwelling unit. 405-1913 calls it an accessory use not rented 'as an apartment or separate dwelling unit' and additions without a density increase use the block-median figures (405-606A(2)). Ask.
